# sample-results: SYNTHETIC data

**Everything in this folder is synthetic.** It was generated by
`generate_synthetic.py` (seeded, so it is reproducible) while the kit was
built, without calling any model. It is not a measurement and not a prediction
of what the labs will show. `SOURCE` says what the folder currently holds.

It exists so the offline parts of the workshop work before anyone has run
anything, or when a pair's runs fail:

| File | Used by | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `export.jsonl` | `./export-results.sh --sample`, `./lab2.sh --sample`, `./lab6.sh --sample`, the board rehearsal | 408 board lines for 10 made-up pairs, ids `SYNTH-01` to `SYNTH-10`, in the RESULTS-SCHEMA.md format |
| `traces/synthetic-*.jsonl` | `./lab4.sh --sample`, `./trace-report.sh` | two stream-json sessions on `report-sort-accents`, one lean and tidy, one bloated with a re-read, a repeated call, a blind retry and a restated plan; the first event is a `synthetic_notice` |
| `lab5-judge/sonnet/s*.json` | `./lab5.sh --sample` | judge scores in `judge.sh`'s output format |
| `lab5-human-scores.csv` | `./lab5.sh --sample` when your own sheet is empty | one made-up pair's hand scores |

The shapes follow Claude Code 2.1.x output and the lab schema; the numbers come
from plausible ranges (a Sonnet session on this repo: roughly 8-16 turns and
0.2-0.5M tokens, ~90% of them cache reads; Haiku cheaper per run but passing
less often on the harder tasks; the synthetic judge leans +0.4 towards
"model" samples). Those choices are the generator's assumptions, visible in
the script. Do not quote them as results.

## Replace it with real data

The facilitator runs `./record-facilitator-run.sh` once during the dry run
(about 18 agent sessions and 8 judge calls on their own plan). It rewrites
`export.jsonl`, `traces/`, `lab5-judge/`, `lab5-human-scores.csv` and `SOURCE`
from the real run and appends a note to this README. Review the traces before
committing them. To go back to the synthetic set:
`python3 sample-results/generate_synthetic.py`.
